scenario: AITA for playing videogames at 2AM on a Friday night. | Tldr: roommate calls me out for play video games at this time if the day. Little context, I live with 4 roommates, each have their own room. Most of them are pretty loud whenever they're home. I always play online videogames when I'm free. Especially these days. I was playing online to today with a couple of friends online. I am usually not very loud, but not very quiet either. Just like an average person having an average phone call. Around 2AM, my roommate knocked on my door, told me he was trying to sleep. He seemed very angry. I know it's fair that I should not be playing, but my friends always play very late and not early. Is it moral to continue playing late but try to keep it quiet?

I know it's fair that I shouldn't be playing so late, but my friends always play very late and not early. So, is it moral to continue playing late but try to keep it quiet? Even though I'm not super loud, it's still enough to be noticeable, especially at 2 AM. I wonder if the time of day plays a role here. 2 AM is quite late, and most people are asleep by then. Even if my friends play late, that doesn't necessarily mean it's okay for me to do the same, especially if it's affecting someone else's sleep. I also think about the fairness aspect. My roommate is trying to sleep, and I'm choosing to play games instead. It's a balance between my hobby and respecting my roommate's need for rest. Alternatively, using headphones could help reduce the noise, but I'm not sure if that's feasible or if it would be quiet enough. Another angle is communication. Maybe I should talk to my roommate about finding a compromise. Perhaps we can agree on certain quiet hours or find a time when it's okay for me to play without interrupting their sleep. I also need to reflect on whether my actions are respectful. Even though I'm not the loudest, the fact that my roommate is upset indicates that my gaming is affecting them. It's important to consider their feelings and adjust my behavior accordingly. In the end, it's about balancing my own activities with the comfort of my roommates. It might be worth making some adjustments to ensure everyone can coexist peacefully.
